mainProgression.description: One of the most famous post-grunge guitar riffs of the 2000s. Matt Roberts arpeggiates open and barre voicings across Bm, G, Em, and an exotic major F# chord borrowed from B Harmonic Minor, creating an addictive, cycling hook that explodes into crushing power chords.

sectionProgressions.description: Clean, staccato picking arpeggiating individual chord tones with snappy bass notes at 135 BPM
Intimate arpeggiated comping supporting Brad Arnold's driving vocal narrative
'If I go crazy, will you still call me Superman?' - massive unmuted power chords ringing with arena drive

sectionProgressions.progression: Bm - G - A - Bm - G - A - F#
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - VI - VII - i - VI - VII - V
sectionProgressions.description: Anthemic ascending progression introducing the subtonic A major chord before resolving to dominant F#

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Dark, brooding tonic minor chord establishing the superhero narrative gravity
G (VI) - Submediant chord providing emotional lift and harmonic expansiveness
Em (iv) - Subdominant minor chord deepening the melancholic tension
F# (V) - Dominant major chord borrowed from B Harmonic Minor (with A# leading tone) pulling forcefully back to Bm
A (VII) - Subtonic chord in the bridge providing classic rock forward momentum

techniques.name: Precision Single-Note Arpeggiation
techniques.description: Picking individual strings in ascending and descending patterns across Bm, G, Em, and F# shapes with clean pick articulation and light palm dampening

notes: Fret standard Bm barre chord on fret 2 of the A string
Strike bass note firmly on beat 1, then pick strings 4, 3, and 2 in clean sequence
Shift quickly to open G major shape, picking low G root followed by upper triads
Execute the F# major triad with crisp finger placement on frets 2, 4, 4, and 3
sequence: Pick B root on fret 2 of A string
Pick frets 4 on D string, 4 on G string, and 3 on B string
Move to G root on fret 3 of low E string
Resolve onto F# major barre chord on fret 2 of low E string
tips: Use a medium plectrum (0.73mm to 0.88mm) for balanced string articulation and flexible attack
Do not rush: maintain an unhurried, steady eighth-note pulse at 135 BPM
Add a subtle touch of analog chorus and delay to expand the stereo field

techniques.name: Heavy Downstroke Power Stabs
techniques.description: Crushing, synchronized downstroke power chord picking during the chorus, locking tight with the kick drum and bass guitar for maximum modern rock impact

notes: Fret B5, G5, E5, and F#5 power chords on strings 6 and 5
Drive downstrokes with aggressive wrist velocity on beats 1, 2, 3, and 4
Emphasize the raised A# in the F#5 chord for dramatic harmonic turnaround
Dampen strings cleanly on the turnaround back to the quiet verse
sequence: Smash B5 on fret 2 of A string with heavy tube distortion
Drop to G5 on fret 3 of low E string
Hit E5 on open low E and fret 2 of A string
Land on F#5 on fret 2 of low E string
tips: Matt Roberts used Gibson Les Pauls into Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifiers and Marshall JCM2000s
Ensure your pick angle is slightly slanted to bite firmly into wound strings
Keep fret-hand pressure relaxed between chord shifts to avoid forearm tension

sections.name: Intro Signature Arpeggio Riff
sections.description: One of modern rock's most recognizable guitar hooks: clean, chiming arpeggios over Bm, G, Em, and F# at 135 BPM.
notes: Clean electric tone with light chorus and studio reverb
Let every chord tone ring out cleanly into the next
Emphasize the major F# turnaround chord on measure 4
Full band explodes on the final repeat

sections.name: Verse 1 Intimate Storytelling
sections.description: 'I took a walk around the world to ease my troubled mind...' - gentle arpeggiated picking beneath Brad Arnold's driving vocal.
notes: Soft, controlled pick attack
Clean transitions between Bm barre and open G shapes
Keep the rhythm flowing steadily at 135 BPM
Prepare pick hand for the massive chorus explosion

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Post-Grunge Explosion
sections.description: 'If I go crazy, will you still call me Superman?' - massive wall-of-sound power chords roar with arena energy.
notes: Full unmuted power chords with heavy distortion
Aggressive downstroke pick velocity
Lock tight with the driving drum snare
Smooth return to the clean verse arpeggio

sections.name: Guitar Solo & Blues-Rock Phrasing
sections.description: Chris Henderson delivers a soaring, lyrical guitar solo featuring crying whole-step bends, singing vibrato, and fast minor pentatonic runs.
notes: Full-step bend on fret 9 of G string up to B
Singing vibrato applied with whole-wrist motion
Fast descending B minor pentatonic run across frets 7 and 9
Slide down into the final explosive chorus

sections.name: Outro Climax & Final Arpeggio Fade
sections.description: Final chorus repetition culminating in a return to the clean, delicate intro arpeggios that fade gently into silence.
notes: Dynamic drop back to clean guitar tone
Delicate fingerpicking on final Bm chord
Let the final chord ring out naturally
Slow studio decay to silence

beginner.title: Chords & Basic Progression
steps: Learn open and barre chord fingerings for Bm, G, Em, and F#
Practice shifting smoothly between Bm and G at 100 BPM

intermediate.title: The Arpeggiated Intro Riff
steps: Master the clean single-note picking pattern across all four chords
Ensure the F# major chord rings with clear pitch accuracy
Execute the dynamic jump into the heavy distorted chorus

advanced.title: Guitar Solo & Complete Performance
steps: Transcribe and perform the expressive guitar solo
Nail the singing whole-step bends and vocal vibrato
Perform the full 3:53 track maintaining rock-solid 135 BPM timekeeping

commonMistakes: Playing F#m instead of F# major, losing the dramatic leading-tone tension from B Harmonic Minor
Muting notes prematurely during the clean intro arpeggio
Rushing ahead of the 135 BPM tempo during the chorus power-chord downstrokes
Over-bending or under-bending notes in the guitar solo
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Bm and F# barre chord finger warm-up drills
10 mins: Slow metronome practice of the intro arpeggio at 95, 115, and 135 BPM
10 mins: Chorus heavy power chord syncopation and dynamic drills
10 mins: Solo transcription study focusing on bend accuracy
focusAreas: Clean pick-hand string isolation during arpeggios
Dynamic contrast between quiet verse picking and arena choruses
Fret-hand thumb positioning for clean barre chord execution
metronomeWork: Set your metronome to 135 BPM to lock in the steady post-grunge tempo
Practice picking strictly on the eighth-note grid to develop rock-solid timing
Ensure the chord changes land squarely on beat 1 without hesitation
